query: Consider the following context: Phonon scattering by SRO precipitates might be expected to reduce scattering times and, therefore, decrease thermal conductivity. In that context, which material can be used for lattice heat conductivity, and why?

generation.hypothesis: High-entropy alloys can be used for lattice heat conductivity due to their unique phonon scattering properties.
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between phonon scattering and lattice thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys is not fully understood.

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the lattice thermal conductivity of a high-entropy alloy and compare it to a simple monatomic element.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the lattice thermal conductivity of the high-entropy alloy is not significantly lower than that of the simple monatomic element, the hypothesis is falsified.

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How do the phonon dynamics of the high-entropy alloy FeCoCrMnNi compare to those of glasses and complex metallic alloys (CMAs), and does it represent a unique class of materials?. System: Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20 (FeCoCrMnNi), a 5-element equiatomic FCC random solid solution. Processing: Polycrystalline samples produced by alloying high-purity elements in an inductively coupled high-frequency levitation furnace, slip-cast into a water-cooled copper mold, and annealed at 1200 °C for 48 h; single crystals grown via the Bridgman technique at 1340 °C with a solidification velocity of 50 mm/h under 200 mbar argon. Test conditions: Measurements performed at temperatures of 3, 15, 100, 200, and 300 K using inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS); energy ranges up to 30 meV and wavevectors covering the Brillouin zone.
